chunks: Al-Ridha عليه السلام was asked about a man who steps in the bathhouse while there are cracks in his feet, then steps on urine and lime, and a black trace from the filth he stepped on enters the cracks. He has washed it, so what should he do regarding it and regarding the foot with which he stepped on it? Is washing sufficient for him, or should he clean between [his nails] with his nails? And he cleans himself and then notices an odor from his nails while seeing nothing.
So he said: “There is nothing upon him because of the odor or the cracks after washing it.”

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha عليه السلام, from whom the ruling is transmitted
key_terms.الرِّيحِ: odor or smell remaining after cleaning
key_terms.الشُّقَاقُ: cracks or fissures in the skin of the feet
key_terms.النُّورَةَ: lime depilatory substance mentioned in the scenario
key_terms.الْبَوْلَ: urine, a source of ritual impurity
key_terms.الْغَسْلُ: washing, the purifying act discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is washing enough if najasah enters cracks in the foot or smell remains under the nails?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on ritual purity when impurity affects cracked skin and the area has been washed. It indicates that after washing, lingering odor or dark traces within cracks do not impose further liability.
